title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing p.16). X is a space and A ⊂ X a closed subspace, the 'nœud' (node). β = {ρ, ρ'} is a two-element set, 'le binaire', which plays the role of the normal 0-sphere of A. Following p.16, a 'maille' structure is defined by cutting X open along A. One takes the double covering à of a neighbourhood boundary, regularly immersed, and glues to obtain X̄ = Dec_β(A,X) together with a map X̄ → X. This map is an isomorphism off A, and over A it is the projection A×β → A. So the preimage of A is two copies A_ρ and A_ρ' of A, the two 'rives' (banks).

This page, first part. (A,β) 'defines a structure of maille with node A and binary β' when (X̄, {A_ρ, A_ρ'}) is a 'feuille topologique'. That is a topological 'sheet' with two distinguished boundary pieces, satisfying conditions a) b) c) of an earlier definition. In modern terms, A is a two-sided, collared codimension-one subspace (a 'wall'). X̄ is X cut along A, and the cut space has boundary A ⊔ A.

Orientation. Orienting the maille means, by definition, orienting the fibre β. Equivalently it means choosing one of A_ρ, A_ρ', or one of ρ, ρ', i.e. one of the two banks making up the binary. In modern language this is a co-orientation of a two-sided hypersurface: a trivialisation, or choice of side, of the normal S^0-bundle. Here that bundle is globally trivialised as A×β.

Compatibility of two mailles (A1, β1 = {ρ1, ρ1'}) and (A2, β2 = {ρ2, ρ2'}) on X:
- a) A1 ∩ A2 = ∅. Then A2 identifies with a part of X̄^(A1,β1) minus A1×β1.
- b) A2 is again a maille (lieu?) in the cut space X̄^(A1,β1). This is the iterated cutting condition.
- c) Let U, V be the two connected components of X̄^(A1,β1) with the banks and A2 removed. The next page says {U,V} then defines something attached to the banks B1, B2.

The figure is an annulus cut along two radial arcs. The top arc A carries banks ρ, ρ'; a bottom arc is the second maille. Cutting along both produces two components U and V.

Margin NB: in all of the above, A1 and A2 are not assumed to be reduced to a point. So the notion is meant for general codimension-one nodes, not only for vertices of graphs.

Purpose. This is the foundation of a combinatorial-topological theory of 'réseaux' (networks / cell-like decompositions, cf. maps and dessins). Surfaces or spaces are built from 'feuilles' glued along 'mailles' with binary data. Compatibility of several cuts is the step needed to cut along a whole system of disjoint walls at once.
errors: Definitions are tentative and incomplete: condition b) breaks off ('est une lieu[?] de ...') and condition c) is only finished on the next page.

The two-component condition c) presupposes the cut space is connected with exactly two components after the second cut. This fails in general (e.g. non-separating second cut). It is presumably intended as part of the definition of compatibility, but it is not stated clearly.

ideas.what: Cutting a space along a two-sided codimension-one subspace A, with the normal data encoded by a 2-element set β; X̄ = Dec_β(A,X) with banks A×β
ideas.modern_name: cutting along a two-sided (collared) hypersurface; split/cut manifold
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and dévissage of surfaces only informally

ideas.what: Orientation of a maille = orientation of the 0-dimensional fibre β = choice of a bank
ideas.modern_name: co-orientation (orientation of the normal S^0-bundle) of a wall

ideas.what: Compatibility of two mailles: disjointness, iterated cutting, and a two-component separation condition
ideas.modern_name: systems of disjoint walls / pants-type decompositions; nested vs transverse walls in wallspaces

missed.claim: An axiomatic 'topological realization of réseaux' via feuilles glued along mailles with binary/orientation data. This is an intended tame-topology foundation for combinatorial maps. The compatibility axioms are left unfinished here.
missed.quote: Orienter la maille, c'est par définition orienter la fibre, i.e. choisir A_ρ — A_ρ', i.e. choisir ρ — ρ' i.e. une des rives qui constituent le binaire.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor documentary point. It shows Grothendieck in 1986 developing a wall/cut formalism for his 'réseaux' program, adjacent to the tame topology of the Esquisse. Mathematically it is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine foundational definitions: cutting along a two-sided hypersurface, co-orientation, and compatibility of disjoint cuts. They are interesting only as documentation of the 1986 réseaux project.
transcription_corrections: '(X̄, {A_ρ, A_ρ'}) est une recollement top.' should read 'est une feuille top.' ('feuille' is underlined).
'rives qui constituent la bordure' should read 'rives qui constituent le binaire'.

Line 3 likely reads 'à nœud A, à binaire[?] β', consistent with p.16 ('de nœud A') and its margin ('β = {ρ, ρ'} le binaire'). 'à l'endroit' is probably a misreading of an underlined word, perhaps 'nœud'.
Under the pairs, the labels are β1 = {ρ1, ρ1'} and β2 = {ρ2, ρ2'}, indicated by underbraces.
In a) the struck 'B_2' / 'définit' is followed by 's'identifie à une partie de X̄^(A,β1) − A1×β1'.
In c), the set removed is ((A1,ρ1) ∪ (A1,ρ1')) ∪ A2 (the transcription's '×' appears to be a crossed or overstruck symbol), and the line below reads 'composantes connexes de'.
